title: Metropolitan Transportation Authority/New York City Transit’s 'third' safety risk assessment (SRA) submitted to FTA in response to Required Action 24-6-001-1

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Metropolitan Transportation Authority/New York City Transit’s 'third' safety risk assessment (SRA) submitted to FTA in response to Required Action 24-6-001-1
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The “third" safety risk assessment (SRA), and related correspondence, submitted to the Federal Transit Administration by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority/New York City Transit” in response to Required Action FTA-24-6-001-1.

For reference, the records are expected to have been produced by the MTA/NYCT in response to a letter of August 19, 2025, signed by Joe Lorenzo, Associate Administrator and Chief Safety officer, Office of Transit Administration and Oversight, Federal Transit Administration, and addressed to Demetrius Crichlow, President, New York City Transit Authority. The letter, with subject "Bringing NYCT into compliance with Required Action FTA-24-6-001-1" stipulated that a Safety Risk Assessment submitted by MTA/NYCT on January 27, 2025 was deficient, and required MTA/NYCT to submit a third revision of the SRA within thirty calendar days of the receipt of that letter. The FTA's letter of August 19, 2025 is posted at the following URL: https://www.transit.dot.gov/about/news/letter-fta-mta-new-york-august-2025

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Noah McClain

Dear Requester, 
The California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) received a Records Request from you on March 11, 2026. 
In your request, you seek the following: "To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

Hello, 

I am seeking copies of the Voluntary Surrender of Peace Officer Certification Forms, POST 2-357 submitted to your department by any officers employed (or now formally employed) by Los Angeles Police Department and Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department since 2022. Include any accompanying documents with the forms. 

Thank you 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Joey Scott 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2238338/" 
Further clarification is required to complete your request: The Affidavit of Separation Form (POST 2-357) is not used by an officer when they surrender their POST certificate(s). The Affidavit of Separation Form (POST 2-357) is submitted by the employing law enforcement agency to notify POST that a peace officer has separated from employment and the reasons for that separation. 
Separation from employment with a particular law enforcement agency does not result in the surrender of POST certificates. 
Therefore, the POST 2-357 form does not document the surrender information that you are seeking. 
The surrender information can be found on POST’s website https://post.ca.gov/Peace-Officer-Certification-Actions where you can use the word “surrender” in the search box and then sort the result in alphabetical order by agency to see which officers from LAPD and LASD have surrendered their certificates. 
Also, the form used for surrenders is the POST 2-358 Form a blank version of this form is attached. 
After reviewing this information if you wish to continue with this request, please provide POST which form you want records on. 
 
  * Do you want the POST 2-357 - Affidavit of Separation Form records. 
  * Do you want the POST 2-358 - Voluntary Surrender of Peace Officer Certification Form records.

POST Records Unit

communications.communication:
Hello, 

Sorry, I meant separation, not surrender. My bad. Yes, please send me completed POST 2-357 forms. Are these records I can request and have released? The records are in the public interest as they inform them why an officer specifically no longer works for a department, specifically in cases of misconduct. Often times, officers retire before disciplinary action is enforced or separate for not cooperating with a misconduct investigation. Officers may end up in other departments or may have a history of misconduct. 

Thank you for your helpfulness and timely response to requests. Other agencies could learn something from you all.

title: Social media guidance 10/07 onward (United States Agency for International Development)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Social media guidance 10/07 onward (United States Agency for International Development)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) From October 7, 2023 to the time that this request is processed: A copy of any official guidance provided to, or created by, the head of social media or communications for this department — specifically, guidance regarding public communications or posts about the Israel/Gaza conflict.

Note 1: These documents may be referred to as guidance documents, social media policy documents, memoranda, letters, notes from meetings, or emails.

Note 2: If you need a keyword search, please search for the following terms:
—“Israel"
—“Gaza"
—“Hamas
—“Palestine"
—“Palestinian"
—"Students for Justice in Palestine"
—“SJP"
—“Chabad
—"Hillel”

Note 3: Please limit the scope of this request to the head of communications/social media for this department.

This FOI request is being filed in pursuit of a time-sensitive news story. Therefore, I ask that my request is expedited. When completing this request, please prioritize whichever records would take the least amount of time to be located and released. I would like these records in electronic format, sent via email or other digital method, and again, please release documents on a rolling basis, as they become available.

If you determine that any of the information qualifies for an exemption from disclosure, I ask you to note whether the exemption is discretionary, and if so whether it is necessary in this case to exercise your discretion to withhold the information. In any event, please provide a signed notification citing the legal authorities on which you rely if you determine that any of the information is exempt and will not be disclosed.

Also, I am a member of the news media as a reporter for Business Insider, and the requested documents are in the public interest and not being made for commercial purposes. Therefore, I ask that all fees are waived in the processing of my request. If fees associated with this request will be in excess of $25, kindly notify me in advance of fulfilling this request. As I am making this request as a journalist and this information is timely, I would appreciate your communicating with me if you have questions regarding this request.

Thanks again, and if there are any questions about my request, can provide any clarification that will help expedite the processing of my request, please contact me at email address. I am also happy to hop on the phone.

I look forward to your reply within 20 business days, as the statute requires and an even more prompt reply if you can make a determination without having to review the records in question.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Best,
Caroline

Once your request is perfected, you will be notified of the FOIA Specialist assigned to process your case.  If you have questions, please contact us at .  Please cite the above-referenced number when corresponding with our office. communications.subject: USAID FOIA REQUEST No. F-00048-24 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email)
communications.communication:
November 06, 2023 Re: USAID FOIA Request No. F-00048-24 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email) Dear Ms.  Haskins: This acknowledges receipt of your November 06, 2023  Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). Specifically, you requested from October 7, 2023 to the time that this request is processed: A copy of any official guidance provided to, or created by, the head of social media or communications for this department — specifically, guidance regarding public communications or posts about the Israel/Gaza conflict. (Date Range for Record Search: From 10/7/2023 To 11/6/2023). FOIA Specialist our request has been assigned to Starr Lewis, FOIA Specialist.  You may contact Starr Lewis by email at slewis@usaid.gov. Please reference the tracking number cited above in any future correspondence. Extending the FOIA’s Time Limits due to Unusual Circumstances The FOIA provides that an agency  may extend its time limits when “unusual circumstances” occur in the processing of a request. See 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B)(i) (2016).  Those “unusual circumstances” are set forth in the statute, 5 U.S.C § 552(a)(6)(B)(iii), and are described as: 1) The need to search for records from field facilities or other locations separate from the office processing the request; 2) The need to search, collect and examine voluminous records; and 3) The need for consultation with another agency. Based upon the records you have requested, we have determined that one or more unusual circumstances will occur during the processing of your request.  Accordingly, your response time-limit has been extended beyond the 20 days required by statute; therefore, 10 additional processing days have been added to your request. To mitigate this action, you may limit the scope of the request so that it can be processed more quickly or to arrange an alternative time to respond. If you have any questions or wish to discuss reformulation or an alternative time frame for the processing of your request, you may contact the assigned FOIA Specialist noted above. You may also contact USAID’s FOIA Public Liaison, Christopher Colbow, at foia@usaid.gov (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) . 
Additionally, you may contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at the National Archives and Records Administration to inquire about the FOIA mediation services offered: Office of Government Information Services National Archives and Records Administration 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001 E-mail: ogis@nara.gov Telephone: 202-741-5770; Toll Free: 1-877-684-6448 Fax: 202-741-5769 Thank you for your interest in USAID. Sincerely, 
Starr Lewis 
FOIA Specialist 
Bureau for Management 
Office of Management Services 
Information and Records Division

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Please provide any and all records captured by the City of Wyoming's Flock Citizen Surveillance System for the following Wyoming City Council Members. This information should also include any connection between the vehicle and the faces/and or identities of these citizens. Additionally, if there are any schematics on the paths these citizens take throughout the city. This information should also include the number of times the license plates have been scanned within the last month. Thank you for your cooperation.

Kent Vanderwood
Mayor

Mayor Pro-Tem

Henry Smith

To Whom It May Concern:

These Citizen Surveillance Cameras are illegal under the 4th Amendment of the US Constitution which prohibits unreasonable searches and seizures.

IF, the Wyoming Police Department can provide any evidence that the Flock cameras that have been installed in the City of Wyoming have reduced crime, please produce analysis on those solved crimes, compared to the  number of times the Flock system has been used by Wyoming Police Department or other Wyoming officials with access. A ratio of "crimes solved" versus "illegal system abused" by Wyoming would be beneficial to the citizens The Wyoming Police Department serves. 

Additionally, please present the list of any and all queries made by agencies or organizations of any kind using the Flock system other than the Wyoming Police Department, if any such as the ATF, DHS, ICE, or any other agency whatsoever, state or federal. 

Additionally, please present a list of any and all businesses in the City of Wyoming, if any, that consented to cameras being installed on their property. 

Thanks

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Massachusetts HHS response
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Communications and correspondence with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services regarding the Aug. 26, 2025, HHS letter requesting the Massachusetts Department of Public Health remove content from the state's Personal Responsibility Education Program curricula and program materials. For reference, the letter can be found here: https://acf.gov/sites/default/files/documents/main/08.26.25-Combined-PREP-Letters.pdf.

I also request internal communications between any Massachusetts Department of Public Health employees about the aforementioned letter. If the content changes were made, I request a copy of the material before it was changed as well as a copy of the material after it was changed.

I additionally request that, if possible, fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, processed by a representative of the news media/press and is made in the process of news gathering and not for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ileana Garnand

Sincerely,

Paul Galante

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Denton Flock Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Related to automated license plate reader (ALPR) or "Flock Safety" camera systems operated by or in partnership with the City:

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, or other instruments between the City of Denton and Flock Safety, Inc., or any related entity, including any amendments or renewals. (No date restriction.)

All invoices, payment records, and purchase orders related to Flock Safety equipment, software, or services. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All data retention policies governing footage, license plate reads, or associated metadata collected by Flock cameras. (No date restriction.)

All written policies, procedures, or general orders governing officer access to, and use of, Flock camera data. (No date restriction.)

All records reflecting the total number of Flock cameras deployed, their locations, and dates of installation. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All records of third-party data sharing, including but not limited to agreements or logs of data shared with other law enforcement agencies, federal agencies, or private parties. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All audit logs, access logs, or query logs reflecting searches of Flock camera data by City employees or contractors. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

All records reflecting complaints, grievances, or legal challenges related to the Flock camera program. (January 1, 2020 through present.)

All communications, including email and internal messaging platform records, between City employees and Flock Safety, Inc. representatives regarding the procurement, deployment, expansion, or renewal of the program. (January 1, 2024 through present.)

Any privacy impact assessments, legal reviews, or internal memoranda regarding the program's compliance with Texas law. (No date restriction.)

If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please identify each withheld document by description, date, author, and recipient in a detailed withholding log, and specify the statutory exception claimed for each.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nayab Warach

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1.The total amount of opioid settlement funds received by Westland City so far. 
2.Financial records of all funds that have been allocated and paid to programs or individuals by Westland City.
3.Evidence of financial invoices, statements, payslips and public records that detail past expenditures of opioid settlement funds in Westland City.
4.Minutes of public meetings regarding how the opioid settlement funds will be spent.
5.Records of correspondence and/or documentation of review and approval processes regarding the allocation and spending of opioid settlement funds.
5.The names of the individuals who will review and approve applications for funding
6. A blank copy of the application and any documentation of the approval process used in review.

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2025 Housing Choice Voucher Landlord HAP Payments
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

An electronic copy of any existing spreadsheet, database export, report, listing, or similar electronic record identifying landlords/payees who received Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) through OHFA's Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program during calendar year 2025.

Please provide the existing electronic record in its native format (Excel, CSV, or similar) if available.

I am specifically seeking landlord/payee names and payment amounts if those fields are contained in the existing record.

I am not requesting tenant names, tenant identifying information, individual HAP contracts, copies of checks, property files, or supporting documents.

To minimize staff time and costs, I am requesting existing electronic records or an existing database export only. I am not asking OHFA to create a new report, calculate totals, summarize records, or conduct additional analysis. I pray these records can be provided free of charge or lowest cost possible since this information will be available for the public to use and see.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety (Covington Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Public reports state that this town is using cameras from Flock Safety (a.k.a. "Flock"), the automatic license plate reader (ALPR) company. For the purposes of this request, when I refer to "Flock products," this includes hardware (Flock License Plate Readers (LPRs), Flock Safety Falcons, Flock Video Cameras, Flock Mobile Security Trailers, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection Devices, Flock Drone as First Responder (DFRs), and Flock Alpha) as well as software (Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Flock FreeForm, Flock Vehicle Fingerprint technology, and the National LPR Network). Source: https://www.flocksafety.com/products

Therefore, pursuant to Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records (dated January 1, 2021 to the time this request is processed):

1. All contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, payment records, budgetary quotes, and related procurement records involving Flock Safety.

2. All training, instructional, presentation, and guidance materials concerning the use of any Flock Safety product or service, including hardware and software. This includes, but is not limited to:
a) Presentations, videos, audio recordings, scripts, manuals, and training materials;
b) Meeting notes discussing the use of Flock products;
c) Technical or operational explanations of how Flock products function; and
d) Internal or external documents used to explain, train on, or promote the use of Flock products.

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Mark Stephens (Eskenazi Health Security)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Mark Stephens (5347-3087)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: SUNY Undergraduate Student Workers (State University of New York at Buffalo)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records or data sufficient to show the number of undergraduate students employed by the university as of August 5, 2026, or for the 2025–26 academic year, broken down, if such data is maintained, by:
(a) Federal Work-Study versus non-work-study student employment; and
(b) employing department or division.

If this information is maintained in an electronic database, I request that it be extracted and provided in spreadsheet format (Excel or CSV) pursuant to Public Officers Law § 89(3)(a). If the university does not maintain data in the categories described above, I request the records in whatever form the data is kept, and ask that you advise me of the categories that are available.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Joe Smith

Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on "Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request" on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000

Case Type:
FOIPA

Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)
The FBI's FOIPA Program is searching the FBI's indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 134 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 523 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,335 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 1,875 days for processing.

communications.subject: (U) USSOCOM 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, 2026-289 and 2026-392 - Acknowledgements
communications.communication:
Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Message Body Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

Dear Ms. Best,

This is in response to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request (copy attached) you submitted to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and it was subsequently referred to U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).  It was assigned USSOCOM FOIA 2026-392.  In addition, the FBI previously referred documents to USSOCOM to review pertaining to this request, and they were assigned as USSOCOM FOIA control numbers 2026-087, 2026-144, 2026-145, and 2026-289.  We apologize that you did not receive acknowledgements from us previously for these other case numbers.  Please refer to these numbers should you have any questions concerning your request.

Your requests are being processed in accordance with procedural requirements promulgated in Department of Defense (DoD) Manual 5400.07, which is available on the internet at: https://open.defense.gov/Portals/23/Documents/FOIA/FOIA_Resources/DoDM%205400.07.pdf?ver=2017-03-15-135646-847.  The actual processing time will depend upon its complexity, whether it involves sensitive records, voluminous records, extensive searches, consultation among DoD components or other agencies, and our administrative workload.

We have placed you in the "News Media" category for fee purposes, which means you are obligated to pay for any duplication costs after the first 100 pages; however, depending on the size of the documents, we may provide the final releases on CD or electronically and no charges would be applicable.

The USSOCOM FOIA Office has a substantial number of pending FOIA cases; therefore, we process requests in a multi-track processing system based on the date of receipt and the amount of work and time involved in processing each request.  We estimate the time for completion to be approximately 4-6 months; it could be more or less.  If you wish to discuss this or have any other questions or concerns, please contact this office at FOIA@socom.mil<mailto:FOIA@socom.mil>.
Regards,
USSOCOM FOIA Team

communications.subject: Wyoming Public Records Act Request: Contract Request: Interfolio (University of Wyoming)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wyoming Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Elsevier relating to the licensing of Interfolio;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, and/or data processing agreements; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Elsevier for faculty information system technology;
and
Assessment documentation such as the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) related to Interfolio. 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Interfolio.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michele Gibney

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Information about the lease of DCR land by Tufts University (Division Of Capital Asset Management And Maintenance)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The current and all prior leases, permits, licenses, occupancy agreements, or other agreements between the Commonwealth/DCR (or its predecessor MDC) and Tufts University concerning the Tufts University sailing facility/boathouse now known as the Lawrence S. and Adele Fleet Bacow Sailing Pavilion at Upper Mystic Lake, approximately 1600 Mystic Valley Parkway, including all exhibits, plans, surveys, amendments, extensions, renewals, and documents defining public-access obligations or the boundaries of the premises.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Jalkut

title: State of Jefferson, Federal Land Management & Rural Grievances — Bureau of Land Management Records (Northern California / Southern Oregon)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: State of Jefferson, Federal Land Management & Rural Grievances — Bureau of Land Management Records (Northern California / Southern Oregon)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request all records maintained by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) concerning the "State of Jefferson" movement and related rural/regional grievances about federal land management in northern California and southern Oregon (including Del Norte, Siskiyou, Modoc, Trinity, and Shasta counties in California and adjacent counties in southern Oregon). Specifically, I seek: (1) correspondence, petitions, resolutions, and public comments received by the BLM from counties, elected officials, or citizens referencing the "State of Jefferson," secession, or state-separation in connection with federal land-management policy; (2) records concerning county "coordination" requests, demands for greater local control over BLM-administered public lands, or disputes over grazing, mining, timber, water, or access in these areas that reference the State of Jefferson movement; (3) BLM responses, briefing papers, or internal analyses addressing the State of Jefferson movement or related land-use conflicts; and (4) records of public meetings or listening sessions where the State of Jefferson or secession was raised. Please provide records from 2013 to the present. Please search under the terms "State of Jefferson," "Jefferson," "secession," "coordination," "local control," "Del Norte," and "Cascadia." I am willing to accept records in electronic format.

Request for Fee Waiver: I request a waiver of all fees for this request. Disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it will contribute significantly to public understanding of how federal public-lands management has intersected with state-separation sentiment in rural counties. This request is not made for commercial purposes; I will make the records freely available to the public and to scholars. This request satisfies the statutory public-interest fee-waiver standard.

If a full fee waiver is not granted, I request that fees be limited as I qualify as a representative of the news media and/or as an educational and noncommercial requester. Please notify me in advance if fees are expected to exceed $25.

Request for Expedited Processing: I request expedited processing on the basis of a compelling need. I certify that the statements in this request are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Friedman

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Robert Decker
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Robert Decker (6819-9836)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.communication:
https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

Given this, I am requesting additional information regarding the disciplinary actions taken against this employee.

Thank you.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Over the past few months, there have been multiple media reports of DOGE staff working in an enclave within GSA offices. This has included staff hired from the Executive Office of the President (EOP), OPM and the Department of Labor, among others. It has even been reported that some DOGE leadership continued to show up for meetings even after departing from government service.

I run a public-interest site that tracks information about DOGE's activities in government in the spirit of transparency. I would like to request visitor logs for this year at the GSA. If this is too extensive a request, I can provide a list of specific visitor names to look for. We can also constrain the request to be from January to the end of June, but I would prefer to instead provide a list of names. Thank you.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris

title: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Manhattan Beach Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Manhattan Beach Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We are working on an article focused on California police departments sharing local data with federal authorities, including ICE via LexisNexis. We identified your agency as part of a South Bay Regional Police Consortium that contracted with LexisNexis for AVCC in or around 2020. This request focuses on data your agency shares with LexisNexis, and interfaces that exist with your agency's RMS/CAD/JMS and LexisNexis's systems, including Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), CommunityCrimeMap.com, or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx)

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]
4) Occasionally we have found consortiums who have negotiated to only share local data with other consortium members, not the 2,400 AVCC federal and local LE subscribers. If you have documentation that your data is only shared locally, please share it. Otherwise you may state there are no responsive documents to item 4. 

We welcome (but do not expect or request) any comments you have about the sharing of local police data with federal authorities via LexisNexis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Steven Catron (Burlington Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Steven Catron (6303-1830)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

title: Complete Code of Alabama — bulk machine-readable copy

communications.subject: Alabama Open Records Law Request: Complete Code of Alabama — bulk machine-readable copy
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Alabama Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

This is a public-records request for the complete enacted text of the Code of Alabama, all titles and chapters, current through the most recent session, in bulk machine-readable form. Three items, all requested:

1. NOW — the consolidated machine-readable source file the State already maintains (XML, database export, or word-processing files). Enacted statutory text only; no publisher annotations.

2. GOING FORWARD — the recurring updated export after each session. In the alternative, and preferably: simply PUBLISH the complete bulk code file as a free public download on the State's own site, once and for all.

3. THE PUBLISHING ARRANGEMENT — any contract/MOU/license between the State and any commercial publisher governing the Code, plus the technical exhibits (format, frequency, delivery method). Administrative/procurement records.

Legal basis: enacted statutes are public-domain government edicts (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org). Electronic delivery only. If you are not the custodian, please identify who is.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

André Natta, a citizen of Alabama, in coordination with GavelSight.

communications.subject: Copy of Code of Alabama
communications.communication:
Mr. Natta,

I am in receipt of your letter dated July 16, 2026, wherein you request a copy of the text of the compete enacted Code of Alabama.

We do not keep a copy of the entire code in a single document or database export, but we do make the entire text of the Alabama code available on our website: www.legislature.state.al.us<http://www.legislature.state.al.us/>. If you click on "Legal Resources" and then on the next page click "Code of Alabama" that will take you to the code directory.  From there you can select any one section of code and select print.  Once you've selected "print" it will allow you to select the entire code for printing to a printer or saving to PDF on your computer.

Alternatively, although I'm not an expert in this field, the following link has details on how to fetch the Code of Alabama text.  As I understand it, you can programmatically grab the code text from the website. I believe you would just need to look at the API for the Code found on this page: https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/api.  This involves paginating through the whole code, grabbing the Sections and extracting the text from those records (preferrable for a program or script to do this for you).  We have no single request that will return the entire Code of Alabama, but you should be able to construct it using the info available on the public API site.

Lastly, our publishing contract is with West Publishing Corporation, but as indicated above, our entire code is readily available to anyone who wishes to view or print it. If you would like a copy of the current contract, then please let me know and I will email you a copy.

Sincerely,


James L. Entrekin, Jr.

General Counsel

Legislative Services Agency

(334) 261-0696

www.lsa.state.al.us<http://www.lsa.state.al.us/>



[LSA Logo.png]



NOTICE OF CONFIDENTIALITY:  This electronic message, including attachments, is for the sole use of the named recipient and may contain confidential or privileged information pursuant to Section 29-6-7.1, Code of Alabama 1975.  Any unauthorized review, use, disclosure, copying, or distribution is strictly prohibited.

Best regards

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Master Retainers and Outside Legal Counsel Services Contracts
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A specific set of public financial and master contract records.The context, firm names, and structural funding parameters for this request are derived directly from the District’s document production under MuckRock Request #R000266-120625 (specifically File: 2023-01-17T152531.000Z_364_Redacted), where former General Counsel Shannon McMinimee detailed the historic shifting of special education litigation files. Because the District has already verified the existence of these specific legal service engagements, locating these core master contracts requires zero extended search time.

RECORDS REQUESTED:A copy of the executed professional services agreement, master retainer, or contract in effect prior to January 4, 2022, detailing the "flat monthly rate" terms for special education legal services handled by the law firm of Porter Foster Rorick LLP.A copy of the executed professional services agreement, contract, or retention agreement in effect between January 3, 2022, and January 31, 2023, with the law firm of Perkins Coie to handle special education due process hearing requests.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & REDACTION CLAUSE:To maximize administrative efficiency and minimize any review burdens on District staff, the requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student, parent, or family member under FERPA.Processing Instruction: This request seeks high-level corporate master vendor agreements and structural flat-rate terms. As this contains zero individual student-specific data, please release the agreements in text-readable PDF format showing the public compensation schedules and firm signatures.

PRA Statutory Compliance Reminder:As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a response is required within five (5) business days. Because this targets localized master firm contracts explicitly identified by General Counsel in Request #R000266-120625, extensive system-wide searches are unnecessary.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

Subject: Technical Processing Specification: Pacific Civil Process Vendor Receipt and Service Log Disclosure (Job No. 575724)

Dear Public Records Officer Sarah Kolpacoff and Bellevue School District Public Records Team,

Regarding the active processing of my request for the "Pacific Civil Process Filing Records (Job No. 575724)," this notice provides specific formatting parameters to assist the records team during the final data review and compilation phase.

To ensure the production provides functional financial transparency while maintaining administrative efficiency, please ensure that the following foundational elements remain fully visible within the produced invoice, billing receipt, or return of service logs:

1. Corporate Vendor and Financial Identifiers: Please leave all line-item operational costs, administrative processing fees, corporate tax numbers, and disbursement totals paid by the District to Pacific Civil Process completely visible.

2. Litigation Descriptive Fields: Factual case identifiers, including the formal court docket number, filing dates, and the standardized narrative description of the service execution at Sammamish High School, are requested to remain unredacted.

3. Complete Exclusion of Student PII: As established in the initial request scope, the District is explicitly directed to apply a localized blackout exclusively to the names, birthdays, student IDs, or other personally identifiable information (PII) of any minor student or parent on the form.

4. Identification of Public Officials: The names and official titles of school administrators, district safety staff, or former legal counsel appearing within the covering correspondence or billing lines are requested to remain visible under standard open-government personnel disclosure guidelines.

5. Itemized Clarification Log: Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210(3), if any specific alpha-numeric field, tracking code, or transaction line item outside of student PII is redacted, please provide the accompanying itemized log specifying the precise regulatory basis for the individual omission.

Thank you for your continued work and diligence in processing this specific transaction log.

Sincerely,  
Kung Fu Joe
